DISPOSITION (orchestrator): closing as `duplicate` (subsumed by e9d5).

The debug agent proved the flake was e9d5's new fixture `effect_spies` patching `socket.socket.connect` via `monkeypatch.setattr` while the autouse `_network_guard` `patch.object` was active; monkeypatch's dict-snapshot teardown re-installed the guard permanently on the worker, so every later `@allow_network` test (test_serve) failed with "Network access is forbidden". It reproduces DETERMINISTICALLY without xdist — the "parallel load" framing was a red herring.

This was introduced AND fixed WITHIN e9d5 (Gerrit change 2436): the broken `monkeypatch` form existed only in pre-merge patchsets (CI runs 33333653370/33332386485/33331343082); the landed commit d46c332c switched to `patch.object` (LIFO-correct) and added the regression test `test_effect_spies_do_not_leak_socket_connect_into_later_tests`. Verified on current origin/main (5c28ce66): deterministic repro no longer fires (9 passed), whole mutate/ dir + test_serve one-worker 684 passed, regression test passes.

Because CI (a gate) caught this on the patchset and it was fixed before merge, it NEVER escaped to main — so it is NOT an escaped plan_defect. Closing `duplicate` linked to e9d5 rather than attributing a spurious escape.

Residual (latent, not active): `_network_guard` depends on future patchers also being LIFO-aware. Filing a low-priority defense-in-depth follow-up (self-healing guard) linked discovered_from this ticket; escalating do-now-vs-leave-filed to the operator. No `--force`.
